source_text: Ἀκούσατε δέ, πῶς καὶ περὶ τῶν κηρυξάντων τὴν διδαχὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ μηνυσάντων τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν προεῤῥέθη, τοῦ προειρημένου προφήτου καὶ βασιλέως οὕτως εἰπόντος διὰ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος· „Ἡμέρα τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐρεύγεται ῥῆμα, καὶ νὺξ τῇ νυκτὶ ἀναγγέλλει γνῶσιν. Οὐκ εἰσὶ λαλιαὶ οὐδὲ λόγοι, ὧν οὐχὶ ἀκούονται αἱ φωναὶ αἰτῶν. Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἐξῆλθεν ὁ φθόγγος αὐτῶν καὶ εἰς τὰ πέρατα τῆς οἰκουμένης τὰ ῥήματα αἰτῶν. Ἐν τῷ ἡλίῳ ἔθετο τὸ σκήνωμα αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτός, ὡς νυμφίος ἐκπορευόμενος ἐκ παστοῦ αἰτοῦ, ἀγαλλιάσεται ὡς γίγας δραμεῖν ὁδόν“. Πρὸς τούτοις δὲ καὶ λόγων ἑτέρων τῶν προφητευθέντων δι᾿ αἰτοῦ τοῦ Δαυῒδ καλῶς ἔχον καὶ οἰκείως ἐπιμνησθῆναι λελογίσμεθα, ἐξ ὧν μαθεῖν ὑμῖν πάρεστι, πῶς προτρέπεται ζῆν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα, καὶ πῶς μηνύει τὴν γεγενημένην Ἡρώδου τοῖ βασιλέως Ἰουδαίων καὶ αἰτῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ Πιλάτου τοῖ ὑμετέρου παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς γενομένου ἐπιτρόπου σὺν τοῖς αὐτοῦ στρατιώταις κατὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ συνέλευσιν, καὶ ὅτι πιστεύεσθαι ἔμελλεν ὑπὸ τῶν ἐκ παντὸς γένους ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ὅτι αὐτὸν υἱὸν καλεῖ ὁ θεὸς καὶ ὑποτάσσειν αὐτῷ πάντας ἐχθροὺς ἐπήγγελται, καὶ πῶς οἱ δαίμονες, ὅσον ἐπ᾿ αἰτοῖς, τήν τε τοῦ πατρὸς πάντων καὶ δεσπότου θεοῦ καὶ τὴν αἰτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐξουσίαν φυγεῖν πειρῶνται, καὶ ὡς εἰς μετάνοιαν καλεῖ πάντας ὁ θεὸς πρὶν ἐλθεῖν τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς κρίσεως. Εἰρηνται δὲ οὕτως· „Μακάριος ἀνήρ, ὃς οὐκ ἐπορεύθη ἐν βουλῇ ἀσεβῶν καὶ ἐν ὁδῷ ἁμαρτωλῶν οὐκ ἔστη καὶ ἐπὶ καθέδραν λοιμῶν οὐκ ἐκάθισεν, ἀλλ᾿ ἢ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ κυρίου τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ αἰτοῦ μελετήσει ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός. Καὶ ἔσται ὡς τὸ ξύλον τὸ πεφυτευμένον παρὰ τὰς διεξόδους τῶν ὑδάτων, ὃ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ δώσει ἐν καιρῷ αἰτοῦ, καὶ τὸ φύλλον αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἀποῤῥυήσεται, καὶ πάντα ὅσα ἂν ποιῇ κατευοδωθήσεται. Οὐχ οὕτως οἱ ἀσεβεῖς, οὐχ οὕτως, ἀλλ᾿ ἤ ὡσεὶ χνοῦς, ὃν ἐκρίπτει ὁ ἄνεμος ἀπο προσώπου τῆς γῆς· διὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἀναστήσονται ἀσεβεῖς ἐν κρίσει οὐδὲ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐν βουλῇ δικαίων, ὅτι γινώσκει κύριος ὁδὸν δικαίων, καὶ ὁδὸς ἀσεβῶν ἀπολεῖται“. „Ινα τί ἐφρύαξαν ἔθνη. καὶ λαοὶ ἐμελέτησαν καινά; (??)αρέστησαν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς, καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ κατὰ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ κατὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ, λέγοντες· Διαῤῥήξωμεν τοὺς δεσμοὺς αἰ τῶν καὶ ἀποῤῥίψωμεν ἀφ᾿ ἡμῶν τὸν ζυγὸν αὐτῶν. Ὁ κατοικῶν ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἐκγελάσεται αὐτούς. καὶ ὁ κύριος ἐκμυκτηριεῖ αὐτούς· τότε λαλήσει πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἐν ὀργῇ αὑτοῦ, καὶ ἐν τῷ θυμῷ αὐτοῦ ταράξει αὐτούς. Ἐγὼ δὲ κατεστάθην βασιλεὺς ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ Σιὼν ὄρος τὸ ἅγιον αὐτοῦ, διαγγέλλων τὸ πρόσταγμα κυρίου. Κύριος εἷπε πρός με· Υἱός μσυ εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε. Αἴτησαι παρ᾿ ἐμοῦ, καὶ δώσω σοι ἔθνη κληρονομίαν σου, καὶ τὴν κατάχεσίν σου τὰ πέρατα τῆς γῆς· ποιμανεῖς αὐτοὺς ἑν ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ, ὡς σκεύη κεραμέως συντρίψεις αὐτοὺς. Καὶ νῦν βασιλεῖς σύνετε, παιδεύθητε πάντες οἱ κρίνοντες τὴν γῆν. Δουλεύσατε τῷ κυρίῳ ἐν φόβῳ, καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε αὐτῷ ἐν τρ(??)μῳ. Δράξασθε παιδείας, μή ποτε ὀργισθῇ κύριος, καὶ ἀπολεῖσθε ἐξ ὁδοῦ δικαίας, ὅταν ἐκκαυθῇ ἐν τάχει ὁ θυμὸς αὐτοῦ. Μακάριοι πάντες οἱ πεποιθότες ἐπ᾿ αὐτόν“.
pass_a_gloss: Hear, how also concerning the ones having preached his teaching and having announced his epiphany, it was spoken beforehand by the aforementioned prophet and king, thus speaking through the prophetic Spirit: Day to day utters a word, and night to night announces knowledge. There are no speeches or words, of which the voices of those crying out are not heard. Into all the earth their sound went out and into the ends of the inhabited world the words of those crying out. He placed his tabernacle in the sun, and he, like a groom coming out of his chamber, will rejoice like a giant to run the way. In addition to these things, we also thought it right and fitting to recall the words of other things prophesied through the Spirit of David, from which you have it to learn how the prophetic Spirit exhorts humans to live, and how it announces the things done by Herod the king of the Jews and the Jews and Pilate your governor who was among them with his soldiers against Christ, and that he was to be believed by humans from every nation, and that God calls him Son and has promised to subject all enemies to him, and how demons, as far as they are able, try to flee the authority of the Father of all and the Lord and of the Spirit of Christ, and how God calls all to repentance before the day of judgment comes. It has been said thus: Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly and did not stand in the way of sinners and did not sit in the seat of the pestilential, but rather in the law of the Lord his will, and in the law of the Lord he will meditate day and night. And he will be like the tree planted by the streams of water, which yields its fruit in its season, and its leaf will not wither, and all that he does will prosper. Not so the ungodly, not so, but like the chaff which the wind blows away from the face of the earth; therefore the ungodly will not rise in judgment nor sinners in the counsel of the righteous, because the Lord knows the way of the righteous, and the way of the ungodly will perish. Why did the nations rage and the peoples devise? The kings of the earth stood, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ, saying: Let us break their bonds and cast away from us their yoke. He who dwells in the heavens will laugh at them, and the Lord will mock them; then he will speak to them in his anger, and in his wrath he will trouble them. But I was established as king by him on his holy mountain Zion, proclaiming the decree of the Lord. The Lord said to me: You are my Son, I have begotten you today. Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession; you will shepherd them with a rod of iron, as the vessels of a potter you will shatter them. And now, kings, understand; all you who judge the earth, be instructed. Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice before him with trembling. Take hold of instruction, lest the Lord become angry and you perish from the way of the righteous, when his wrath is kindled in a short time. Blessed are all who trust in him. Take hold of instruction.

pass_b_english: Listen to how it was foretold, through the prophetic Spirit, concerning those who preached his teaching and announced his appearing, by the prophet and king already mentioned: Day after day pours forth speech, and night after night declares knowledge. There is no speech, nor are there words, whose voice is not heard. Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world. In the sun he has set his tent, and he, like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, rejoices like a giant to run his course. (Psalm 19:2-5) In addition to these, we also deemed it right and fitting to recall other words prophesied through the Spirit of David, from which you can learn how the prophetic Spirit urges human beings to live, and how it announces what was done by Herod the king of the Jews and the Jews and Pilate, your governor among them, with his soldiers against the Christ; and that he was about to be believed by people from every nation; and that God calls him Son and has promised to subject all enemies to him; and how the demons, as far as they are able, try to flee the authority of the Father of all and Master, God, and of the Spirit of Christ; and how God calls all to repentance before the day of judgment arrives. It has been said thus: Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in the seat of the pestilential; but his delight is in the law of the Lord, and on his law he will meditate day and night. And he will be like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in its season, and its leaf does not wither, and whatever he does prospers. Not so the ungodly, not so; rather, they are like chaff which the wind drives away from the face of the earth. Therefore the ungodly will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the counsel of the righteous; for the Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the ungodly will perish. (Psalm 1:1-6) Why did the nations rage, and the peoples devise new things? The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ, saying: Let us break their bonds and cast their yoke from us. He who dwells in the heavens will laugh at them, and the Lord will mock them; then he will speak to them in his anger, and in his wrath he will trouble them. But I was established as king by him on Zion, his holy mountain, proclaiming the decree of the Lord. The Lord said to me: You are my Son, today I have begotten you. Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession; you will shepherd them with a rod of iron, as a potter's vessels you will shatter them. (Psalm 2:1-9) And now, kings, understand; be instructed, all you who judge the earth. Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice before him with trembling. Take hold of instruction, lest the Lord become angry and you perish from the way of the righteous, when his wrath is kindled quickly. Blessed are all who trust in him. Take hold of instruction. (Psalm 2:10-12)
notes: The translation aims to follow the Greek text closely, without omitting or adding words.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text, including the difficult/corrupt passages (e.g., '??αρέστησαν' and 'τρ(??)μῳ'). Pass A and Pass B both handle the text faithfully. Pass B correctly identifies the Psalm citations (Psalm 19:2-5, Psalm 1:1-6, Psalm 2:1-9, Psalm 2:10-12) which correspond to the quoted Greek scripture. The final repetition 'Δράξασθε παιδείας' is included in both translations.
